posts.title: neil patels reco's & some of my prompts
posts.content:
If youre not familiar Neil patel grew his bootstrapped digital marketing companies to $100M a year. Kinda nuts.

he just posted this article that im excited to try out.

the challenge with ai writing is that most of its garbage

but the future puts a premium on authenticity and being human...

so im always on the lookout for new tools to try.

you can definitely get high quality writing out of using specific prompts

i use the following for short responses (1-4 sentences) whether it be email, or replies to stuff.

i bind "!gptconcise" as a text expander so that when i type it i get the following as a suggestion from mac:

````
I want you to edit my writing. I'll share an excerpt with you to edit as follows:

- Make it more clear and more concise

- Use simple words.

- Give me 3 variations.

Here's the excerpt:
```

It tends to give an authoritative one, a "crisp" one, and a friendly one.

When it comes to longer form writing, I've been using hubspot's templates for seo writing which include 5 different styles

i cant list them all off the top of my head but i use the Step-By-Step actionable guide one.

come to think of it i have a whole airtable database of these..

i think what ill do is set up a [make.com](http://make.com) automation that slow drips them into the skool so that its not just this overwhelming wave of content at once

i find that annoying personally

my X account bookmarks page is littered with a ton of prompts ill never use

and i will say its important to filter who is posting the stuff

ai is hot, people will spam content without even using it or without even making money with it

posts.title: multi-agentic flow for researching winning playbooks from $100m entrepreneurs
posts.content:
im scaling my agency to $100k/mo and want to find entrepreneurs who've done that before

so i typically would research them...

watch videos

take notes...

and thats still valuable no doubt

but i wanted to see how far i could push ai using a few different tools

because the output of what i want to learn is pretty much the same for any entrepreneur

what i want to know
[ol:1]- what niche did they start in- what niche are they in now- how long did it take them to get to where they are now- what tactics did they do each year, and what amount of $$$ did they generate during that period- what are the SPECIFIC daily actions they took.. eg. SEO & Content planning isnt helpful.. 5x 1,000-1,500 word keyword-researched listicle-style blog posts + reaching out to high domain authority ranking sites in their niche is helpful- if you cant find the specifics of the tactic in the youtube video, go research using web - timeline of their growth over time

btw in ai/tech world this is known as structured json output which gives the ai a set of instructions it needs to fill out in order to complete its job

which would look something like this:

(if your not technical, dont worry just gloss over this part)

interface CreatorGrowthAnalysis {
initialNiche: string; // The niche they started in
currentNiche: string; // The niche they are in now
timeToSuccess: string; // How long it took them to get to their current level
yearlyTactics: YearlyTactics\[\]; // A breakdown of tactics and revenue by year
specificDailyActions: string\[\]; // Granular daily actions they took
researchRequired: boolean; // Indicates if additional research beyond the video was needed
growthTimeline: GrowthEvent\[\]; // A timeline of their growth over time
}

interface YearlyTactics {
year: number;
tactics: string\[\]; // Specific strategies used during this period
revenueGenerated: number; // Amount of $$$ generated that year
}

interface GrowthEvent {
year: number;
milestone: string; // Key events in their growth journey
